title: ClickHouse scale-up: vertical VM resize (RAM) on a node
description: The nexus-cli scale-up verb (change CPU/RAM/disk on an existing VM -- vertical). Demonstrates the generic vmrun stop -> .vmx memsize edit -> start -> verify flow on ch-keeper-1 (2 GB -> 3 GB). scale-up is cluster-aware: it refuses to resize a node holding a critical role mid-operation without an explicit override.

observe.what: current RAM ~2000 MB (the right-sized 2 GB keeper, vms.yaml)
graceful guest shutdown (VMware Tools); a non-leader Keeper going down keeps the quorum at 2/3 (still quorate)
.vmx memsize rewritten to 3072 MB; VM powered back on

steps.command: ssh -i $NEXUS_SSH_KEY nexusadmin@192.168.70.41 'free -m | awk "/Mem:/ {print \$2}"; exec 3<>/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/9181; printf "mntr\n" >&3; timeout 3 cat <&3 | grep zk_server_state'

observe.what: RAM now ~3072 MB AND the keeper rejoined the quorum (zk_server_state=follower/leader) -- vertical resize complete + cluster healthy

whatProves: scale-up resizes a node's RAM via the generic vmrun stop -> .vmx edit -> start path and the node cleanly rejoins the cluster. Cluster-aware: a Keeper follower (or a data replica whose shard has a surviving replica) can be resized with no service impact; a sole-surviving member would require an explicit override.
